title: Bayesian modeling estimates configuration-dependent uncertainty in printed PLA bending
summary: A Research Square preprint trained a Bayesian physics-informed neural network on bending data from 60 groups of printed PLA specimens and combined it with finite-element simulation. In ten within-study validation configurations, predicted uncertainty varied by raster angle and infill, with the 60-degree and reduced-infill configurations exceeding twice the estimated variation of the 0-degree configuration. All ten experimental validation values lay within the reported 95% intervals, but the sample is too small to establish precise uncertainty calibration. The result is limited to the studied printer, material and bending conditions, without separate-team replication or demonstrated service reliability.
ai_technology: Bayesian physics-informed neural network with Monte Carlo dropout embedded in finite-element analysis

evidence.tested: The PINN was developed from experimental data for 60 FDM polylactic-acid specimen groups, with ten independent configurations evaluated. Reported R² was 0.9935, MAPE 1.85%, and 95% confidence intervals contained all ten experimental validation values. Reliability analysis estimated coefficient-of-variation uncertainty of 3.8–9.0% across configurations and corresponding safety factors of 1.11–1.30.
evidence.unknown: The ten configurations are within-study validation, not a separate-team replication. Sample size is limited; the results do not establish transfer to other printers, materials, component geometries, or load/service conditions.
evidence.ai_role: A physics-constrained neural network with Monte Carlo dropout estimates flexural-modulus distributions; sampled moduli are propagated through finite-element simulations to estimate configuration-dependent prediction uncertainty.

source_review.scope: Source-provenanced original Research Square v1 full PDF/text: posting metadata, affiliations, learned operation, validation design, reported result and limitations.
